# Clay CLI

> Clay CLI (`@panphora/claycli`, command `claycli`) lets an AI agent read and edit plain HTML files hosted on hyperclay.com. It runs locally as an MCP server for Claude Code, Cursor and Claude Desktop, and as a command for scripts.

## Setup (MCP and sign in)

Requires Node 20.18.1 or later.

Sign in and paste an agent key when asked:

```bash
npx -y @panphora/claycli login
```

Add the MCP server to Claude Code:

```bash
claude mcp add clay -- npx -y @panphora/claycli mcp
```

Cursor (`.cursor/mcp.json`) and Claude Desktop (`claude_desktop_config.json`):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "clay": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@panphora/claycli", "mcp"] }
  }
}
```

Options and session commands:

* Pass `mcp --read-only` to offer only the 10 reading tools.
* Check sign in state: `npx -y @panphora/claycli status`
* Sign out: `npx -y @panphora/claycli logout`

## Hosted MCP option (no install)

Hyperclay runs a hosted MCP server at `https://hyperclay.com/mcp` for Claude Code, Claude.ai, Claude Desktop, Cursor and ChatGPT. Setup for each client is at https://hyperclay.com/docs/agents/.

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http hyperclay https://hyperclay.com/mcp
claude mcp login hyperclay
```

Every tool except `publish_site` works on both. `publish_site` requires Clay CLI because the hosted server cannot read local files on your computer.

## The 18 MCP tools

HTML files can be at most 8 MB. Large files are read in pieces: an outline first, then selected parts, with focused edits applied through `edit_document`.

### Read (5 tools, all included in `--read-only`)

* `list_documents` (read only): HTML files the key can reach.
* `read_document` (read only): Whole HTML file when small, or an outline, or parts selected by CSS selector or character range.
* `outline_document` (read only): Element tree with selector paths and sizes.
* `find_in_document` (read only): Text or regular expression matches with the surrounding element.
* `read_data` (read only): The page's structured data.

### Change (4 tools)

* `edit_document`: Replace exact text in the version read.
* `save_document`: Save a whole HTML file.
* `create_document`: Create a new HTML file at a path such as `notes/plan.html`. Missing folders are created. Refused if anything is already there.
* `write_data`: Change the page's structured data.

### History (3 tools; `list_versions` and `read_version` are included in `--read-only`)

* `list_versions` (read only): Version history of an HTML file.
* `read_version` (read only): Content of a saved version.
* `restore_version`: Restore an earlier version.

### Sites and addresses (6 tools; `list_sites`, `list_files` and `domain_status` are included in `--read-only`)

* `list_sites` (read only): Site folders the key can reach, with each site's address, home page and page count.
* `list_files` (read only): Folders, HTML files and other files under a folder.
* `publish_site`: Upload a local folder as a site. Sends only what changed, never deletes files that exist only on hyperclay.com, and claims the subdomain last.
* `claim_subdomain`: Give an HTML file or a site folder its public address at `<name>.hyperclay.com`.
* `add_domain`: Add a custom domain to an HTML file or a site folder, and return the two DNS records to set.
* `domain_status` (read only): Each custom domain, whether it is active, and the DNS records it needs.

## Agent keys and safety

* Create an agent key in the Hyperclay dashboard: account menu, then "Agent keys…".
* A key has a name, can be limited to one team or one folder, and has one of three access levels: reading, changing content, or full editing.
* Revoke a key at any time. "Recent activity" in the Agent keys dialog shows what each key changed.
* The agent acts as the owner, with no more access than the owner has.
* Saved locally in `~/.config/claycli/credentials.json` (readable only by the owner), never accepted on the command line, and never printed. Set `CLAY_CLI_KEY` in the environment as an alternative.
* Every write is checked against the version read; concurrent edits cause the write to be refused until the agent reads again.
* HTML file edits are saved in version history as "Recorded by you through <key name>". Replaced files keep old bytes as a backup.
* Agents cannot delete, rename, move or share anything, cannot make a private page public, cannot remove a custom domain, and cannot change a subdomain once set.
* Saves containing an agent key or OAuth token are refused.
* Rate limit per key: at most 60 page saves and 300 file writes per minute.

## Command line usage

An HTML file is `hyperclay:<id>` or its `hyperclay.com` URL. File commands accept `--json`. Without a global install, run `npx -y @panphora/claycli <command>`.

```bash
claycli list
claycli read hyperclay:123 --outline
claycli read hyperclay:123 --select 'main > section'
claycli edit hyperclay:123 --find 'Draft' --replace 'Final' --if-match <etag>
claycli create notes/plan.html --file ./plan.html
claycli versions hyperclay:123
claycli subdomain hyperclay:123 my-tool
npx -y @panphora/claycli publish ./maya demos/maya --subdomain maya --dry-run
```

## Compatibility and rename

* Works with hyperclay.com. Support for HTML Clay and Hyperclay Local desktop apps comes in a later version.
* Previously named Clay Agent (`@panphora/clay-agent`, command `clay-agent`). `npx -y @panphora/clay-agent` forwards every command to Clay CLI and stays current, saved keys and `CLAY_AGENT_KEY` continue to work, and existing MCP configs need no changes.
